# **A Unified QMINIWASM Framework: Bridging Qutrit Stabilizer Formalisms and Extreme-Edge Ternary AI**

## **Executive Summary**

The prevailing trajectory of artificial intelligence research has been inextricably bound to the scaling of continuous-variable architectures, characterized by billions of high-precision floating-point parameters optimized via backpropagation. However, this paradigm is rapidly approaching an inescapable thermodynamic asymptote. The energy expenditure required to execute 32-bit floating-point (FP32) matrix multiplications—and more critically, the energy required to ferry these uncompressed tensors across the von Neumann bottleneck between Dynamic Random-Access Memory (DRAM) and the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)—fundamentally precludes the deployment of frontier intelligence on energy-starved edge devices. To circumvent this limitation, the field must undergo a phase transition from continuous to highly quantized, discrete computational models. The QMINIWASM project represents this exact transition, manifesting as a unified, rigorous framework that entirely eliminates floating-point arithmetic in favor of a 1.58-bit ternary state space.

The central, overarching thesis of the QMINIWASM framework is inextricably grounded in the mathematics of quantum information theory, specifically the Gottesman-Knill theorem. The theorem provides a rigorous mathematical proof that any quantum circuit restricted exclusively to the Clifford group of gates can be simulated on a classical Turing machine in polynomial time, offering no exponential quantum speedup. By establishing a strict mathematical isomorphism between the classical 1.58-bit ternary state space (![][image1]) and the quantum computational basis of a three-level qutrit system, the framework demonstrates that highly entangled, topological updates in a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) routing paradigm can be treated exactly as a qutrit Clifford circuit. Consequently, this quantum-inspired routing logic can be simulated classically with absolute algorithmic efficiency using a Stabilizer Tableau mapped over the Galois field ![][image2].

This document exhaustively details the architectural pipeline necessary to realize this unification. It provides a rigorous mapping of data ingestion mechanisms through Absolute Mean (Absmean) quantization and Ternary Locality-Sensitive Hashing (TLSH) for continuous-to-discrete dimensionality reduction. It mathematically proves the optimal memory embedding of base-3 variables into base-2 memory, demonstrating how exactly five trits are compressed into a single 8-bit byte to achieve an unprecedented 99.06% Shannon entropy efficiency. Furthermore, the report delineates the in-situ execution of Modulo-3 arithmetic via the Flash-Cosmos paradigm, utilizing Multi-Wordline Sensing directly within NAND flash memory. These hardware mechanics execute efficiently under a universal WebAssembly (WASM) runtime that entirely bypasses Floating-Point Units (FPUs). Finally, the framework replaces backpropagation with a teacherless Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) pipeline, leveraging Tropical Geometry, the max-plus semiring, and the Forward-Forward algorithm. This synthesis reveals that the Top-K MoE routing isomorphism generates "Combinatorial Depth," delivering a complete, rigorous blueprint for the extreme-edge deployment of highly sparse, highly expressive AI models.

## **The Thermodynamic Imperative and the Quantum-Classical Isomorphism**

### **Thermodynamic Limits of Continuous-Variable Deep Learning**

Standard continuous-variable neural networks are fundamentally bounded by Landauer’s principle of information erasure and the practical energetic realities of modern Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) logic. A single 32-bit floating-point multiply-accumulate (MAC) operation consumes approximately 3.7 picojoules (pJ) of energy. However, retrieving the 32-bit operands from off-chip DRAM consumes upwards of 640 pJ to 1000 pJ—an energetic penalty two orders of magnitude greater than the arithmetic itself. In deep neural networks with billions of parameters, this von Neumann bottleneck ensures that the dominant thermodynamic cost is not computation, but rather data movement.

To overcome this, 1.58-bit neural networks constrain their parameters exclusively to a discrete ternary alphabet of ![][image1]. This extreme quantization forces the network to completely abandon floating-point matrix multiplication in favor of integer addition and subtraction. The introduction of the ![][image3] state is not a trivial algebraic optimization; it provides the network with an explicit, native feature-filtering mechanism. When a weight evaluates to zero, the associated input is not propagated during the forward pass. This dynamically induces a high degree of structural sparsity, meaning the hardware completely skips the execution cycle for that parameter, allowing the architecture to bypass the traditional dense multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations entirely.1

In stark contrast, the restricted ![][image1] weights and activations represent the discrete computational basis states of a bounded qutrit Hilbert space ![][image5].

The mapping between the classical domain and the quantum domain is formally defined over the Galois field ![][image2]. This pipeline operates directly at the sensor or edge-ingestion level.

## **In-Situ Execution & Edge Deployment**

Deploying the qutrit-stabilizer simulation and massive arrays of dense ternary vectors on power-constrained edge devices mandates completely overcoming the von Neumann bottleneck. The energy expended shuttling multi-megabyte parameter blocks between the Solid-State Drive (SSD), DRAM, and the CPU cache must be eliminated. The QMINIWASM framework mitigates this physical constraint via in-situ processing directly within the non-volatile storage arrays.

### **Flash-Cosmos and Multi-Wordline Sensing**

Active mathematical calculations for the framework are driven directly inside the NAND flash memory using the **Flash-Cosmos** (Flash Computation with One-Shot Multi-Operand Sensing) hardware paradigm. Modern 3D NAND flash memory arrays feature vertical string topologies that connect multiple floating-gate transistors. This physical alignment inherently supports massively parallel analog logic.17

In standard architectures, flash arrays only transfer binary data out to peripheral sensing latches (S-latches) and data latches (D-latches) upon a singular row read.17 The Flash-Cosmos paradigm introduces a technique called Multi-Wordline Sensing (MWS). By activating multiple wordlines (WL) concurrently along the same string, the threshold voltages of the vertical storage cells interact analogously at the bitline level. This aggregate voltage shift effectively computes bulk bitwise boolean operations (AND, OR) natively within the silicon, without ever transferring the operands out of the cell.11

This analog superposition of voltages is stabilized through Enhanced SLC Programming (ESP). ESP manipulates the charge-trapping programming voltages to expand the distribution margins between the binary states, ensuring zero read-disturb bit-errors during the aggressive multi-wordline activation phase.11

### **Binary Coded Ternary (BCT) Modulo-3 Logic Synthesis**

To perform ternary neural network operations using binary flash memory, the data must be properly aligned. During active Flash-Cosmos inference, the 5-trit dormant storage format (which is highly dense but computationally opaque) is transiently unpacked into a **Binary Coded Ternary (BCT)** format. Under BCT, each individual trit ![][image87] is represented by a dual-bit parallel sequence ![][image88], designated as the High and Low bits.20

| Ternary Value (1.58-bit) | BCT High Bit (AH​) | BCT Low Bit (AL​) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **\+1** | 0 | 1 |
| **0** | 0 | 0 |
| **\-1** | 1 | 1 |

The fundamental computational advantage of the BCT format is that it mathematically dissects complex integer Modulo-3 arithmetic into rudimentary bit-serial logic gates—precisely the exact boolean operations (XOR, AND, OR) natively supported by the Flash-Cosmos MWS topology.11

Modulo-3 addition (![][image89]), which avoids the cascading latency of standard binary carry chains, can be completely synthesized using native bitwise operators.22 The computation of the High and Low bits ![][image90] of the output sum is resolved via equations derived directly from ternary truth tables:

By executing these logic gates via sequential MWS command pulses, the NAND flash controller aggregates billions of vector additions in-situ. This architectural synthesis decreases data transfer energy consumption by upwards of ![][image93] and precipitates a ![][image94] algorithmic speedup relative to traditional host-centric CPU architectures.11

### **WebAssembly (WASM) Universal Runtime**

The orchestration of these in-situ flash commands, the Stabilizer Tableau matrix updates, and the overarching neural logic is governed by a lightweight WebAssembly (WASM) execution layer. Because 1.58-bit arithmetic models and qutrit Clifford operations rely entirely on discrete integer values (modular addition, XOR arrays, bit-shifting), the WASM runtime orchestrator is compiled to explicitly bypass power-hungry Floating-Point Units (FPUs).

Control instructions map uniformly down to the basic Arithmetic Logic Units (ALUs). This guarantees platform-agnostic, deterministic execution across heterogeneous hardware—whether the framework is running on a low-power embedded ARM microcontroller, an edge IoT sensor, or natively interfacing with the NVMe SSD controller driving the Flash-Cosmos analog logic.

## **Teacherless Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) via Tropical Geometry**

To achieve true on-device autonomy and continual learning at the extreme edge, the architecture must excise conventional gradient descent and backpropagation from the training protocol. Backpropagation relies on the chain rule, which is mathematically non-local; it requires storing massive, high-precision intermediary activation matrices in memory to compute continuous gradients, rendering it thermodynamically unviable for edge hardware. Instead, the QMINIWASM framework unifies Teacherless Self-Supervised Learning (SSL), Tropical Geometry, and the Forward-Forward algorithm to learn exclusively via discrete forward passes.

### **Tropical Geometry and the Max-Plus Semiring**

The topological expressivity of the Mixture-of-Experts routing network is formally defined and optimized using the mathematics of Tropical Geometry. Tropical algebra functions over the *max-plus semiring* ![][image95], an algebraic structure where the standard operations of addition and multiplication are radically redefined. In this semiring, tropical addition is the maximum operator, and tropical multiplication is scalar addition:

![][image96]  
![][image97]  
24

In standard dense neural networks, output logits are evaluated via continuous linear algebra, mapping hyperplanes across Euclidean space. In the MoE paradigm, however, the router evaluates an array of experts and strictly identifies the ![][image98] largest activations. This Top-K routing mechanism acts as a discrete indicator function. Mathematical analysis reveals that this Top-K routing mechanism is perfectly algebraically isomorphic to the *k-th elementary symmetric tropical polynomial* within the max-plus semiring.26

This tropical isomorphism fundamentally redefines the theoretical capacity of the neural network. In continuous deep learning, expressivity scales linearly with the width of the layers. However, the tropical polynomial proves that the MoE routing hyperplanes partition the discrete input space into the Normal Fan of a high-dimensional geometric object known as a *Hypersimplex*. The geometric capacity (the number of distinct linear regions the network can identify) of this partition scales combinatorially by the binomial coefficient ![][image99], where ![][image100] is the total number of available experts and ![][image101] is the active routing subset.26

This theoretical breakthrough proves the axiom that **"Sparsity is Combinatorial Depth."** It demonstrates that 1.58-bit models do not suffer from the capacity collapse usually associated with extreme quantization. The models retain immense *Combinatorial Resilience* because the physical transversality of the routing cones preserves the metric geometry of the data manifold, mimicking the expressivity of massive models without requiring floating-point depth.26

### **The Tropical Inner Product & Forward-Forward (FF) Optimization**

Because continuous geometric metrics—such as traditional cosine similarity—are non-viable in the discrete max-plus semiring and integer-only edge environments, the framework introduces the **Tropical Inner Product**.

By evaluating geometric distances via the max-plus operation ![][image102], the Tropical Inner Product is mathematically proven to strictly obey the triangle inequality constraints necessary for valid metric-space embeddings. It acts as an optimal, computationally lightweight surrogate for traditional continuous dot products.28 This metric mathematically reduces the ![][image103] metric nearness problem, accelerating similarity calculations directly by transforming the loss objective into a continuous optimization task that can be computed using ALUs.

This discrete metric seamlessly integrates with the **Forward-Forward (FF) algorithm** and Non-Parametric Instance Discrimination (NPID). Instead of propagating errors backward from a final global loss function, the FF algorithm evaluates parallel forward passes. One pass processes "positive data" (real, uncorrupted input mappings), while the other processes "negative data" (corrupted or intentionally misrouted mappings generated via NPID).28

Utilizing the Tropical Inner Product, each hidden layer evaluates its own localized "goodness" score independently. If a local MoE routing pathway maximizes the tropical goodness on positive data relative to the negative data, its local ternary weights are structurally reinforced via local Hebbian-style updates. This methodology completely decouples layer training, entirely averts the vanishing gradient problem inherent in quantized networks, and permits continuous, streaming, teacherless learning exclusively at the extreme edge.

## **Conclusion**

The QMINIWASM framework constitutes a rigorous, exhaustive bridging of theoretical quantum physics, abstract algebra, and embedded silicon engineering. By formally anchoring the mathematical topology of discrete Mixture-of-Experts routing within the rigid bounds of the Gottesman-Knill theorem, the architecture proves that highly sophisticated neural topologies can be interpreted and executed as classically simulatable qutrit Clifford operations. The ![][image26] efficiency of the Stabilizer Tableau over the Galois field ![][image2] completely eliminates the exponential constraints associated with probabilistic routing.

Through the synergistic application of Absolute Mean quantization, Shannon-optimal 5-trit-to-8-bit byte packing, and TLSH dimensionality reduction, the framework forcefully translates continuous-variable deep learning into pure discrete mathematics. Operating entirely via bitwise logic and in-situ Modulo-3 arithmetic within NAND Flash-Cosmos memory—and governed autonomously by the max-plus semiring mechanics of Tropical Geometry and the Forward-Forward algorithm—the architecture successfully circumvents the thermodynamic limitations of contemporary von Neumann topologies. This unified, physically precise paradigm delivers a robust, scalable, and inherently sparse framework capable of maintaining exponential combinatorial depth entirely at the extreme edge, inaugurating the next phase transition in artificial intelligence deployment.
